35d924813e8f8450: Global consultancy PwC says IT departments struggling to secure funding for ERP upgrades should make the expected benefits of AI part of their pitch.

The Oracle and SAP mega-partner told El Reg that a "clean core" – modern enterprise applications with fewer customizations embedded in the underlying system – makes deploying AI agents easier. Selling that prospect, rather than incremental improvements to existing processes, could help IT leaders justify a migration.

Oracle and SAP are both trying to persuade customers to move from established ERP systems to newer platforms. For SAP, that means S/4HANA, preferably in the cloud. For Oracle, it means Fusion Cloud Applications. Moving from ECC or E-Business Suite, respectively, can involve root-and-branch changes to technology and business processes, rather than a straightforward software upgrade.

Thousands of organizations still rely on these aging, often heavily customized systems. IT leaders struggle to justify a costly, time-consuming migration when the reward appears to be doing the same meat-and-veg business processes slightly better. For example, a survey of SAP users last year found that 95 percent said building a positive case for migration required substantial effort or was genuinely challenging.

Speaking to The Register, Jennifer Colapietro, PwC digital core modernization platform leader, said: "You're seeing it a lot more as part of the rationale for the business case for why they should upgrade, answering the question: 'Why now? What should we prioritize?' Certainly, AI and getting the value of AI, a key business case justification for that.

"Folks have budgets for ERP, but now [funding for transformation is] being split because they also have budgets for AI. But there's synergies across them. If you look at moving to a clean digital core ERP, that will help them to realize the AI value faster... be able to turn on AI and be able to start to automate a lot of the processes and implement the agents. That helps to build the business case."

SAP recently introduced Joule 2.0 while Oracle has announced Fusion Claw. With both of these new technologies, the vendors are promising customers they can build AI agents to automate business processes and perform some work that was previously done by humans. Colapietro argued that moving to more modern platforms makes deploying AI agents easier and more effective than adding AI capabilities around legacy systems.

"It is more challenging to apply AI to the older systems. We focus on the importance of a clean digital core as the foundation for getting the value and effectiveness out of AI and scaling AI responsibly. I think that's given," she said.

An ERP replacement isn't the only route to AI, however. European home improvement retailer Kingfisher – which owns the B&Q brand in the UK – eschewed SAP's overtures to upgrade its ECC system, despite encroaching deadlines. Mainstream maintenance for supported ECC 6.0 versions ends in December 2027, with optional extended maintenance through 2030 at a premium of two percentage points on the existing maintenance base.
Kingfisher opted instead for third-party support from Rimini Street, building an AI strategy around its existing ERP system using a combination of technology from Databricks and Google.
AI might help sell an ERP migration to the board. It doesn't make replacing the ERP system a prerequisite. ®

c586989ecb966c72: The Investigatory Powers Tribunal (IPT) has confirmed that the UK government served Apple with a secret Technical Capability Notice (TCN), rejecting the Home Office's argument that acknowledging its existence would damage national security.
The order has been widely reported as demanding access to end-to-end encrypted iCloud data.
The three judges pointed to extensive public reporting, statements by US officials, and media briefings they concluded had been authorized by the UK government.
The Home Office had previously adopted its "neither confirm nor deny" (NCND) policy, as is standard when discussing national security matters.
The story broke in February 2025, when The Washington Post reported that the Home Office had demanded an iCloud backdoor the previous month.

A TCN is a notice issued under the Investigatory Powers Act 2016, which compels recipients, such as tech companies, to implement technical changes that facilitate the UK government's legal surveillance powers.

For Apple, a company that has long made privacy central to its marketing, and famously rejected an FBI order to break open an iPhone to assist a terror probe, being served the TCN meant it either had to somehow defy a legal order issued by the UK, or undermine the encryption technology that customers expected.

While it remained officially unconfirmed at the time, Apple's decision to revoke Advanced Data Protection (ADP) for UK users in February 2025 was widely interpreted as indirect confirmation of the demand.

At the same time, US policymakers urged then-director of national intelligence Tulsi Gabbard to oppose the UK's demands under the assumption that they also sought to backdoor Apple's data in a way that would affect US citizens.
In August 2025, Gabbard announced that the UK had agreed to drop its demand for access to Americans' encrypted data. ADP is still available to users in the US.

Apple's ADP extends end-to-end encryption to additional categories of iCloud data, including backups, photos, and notes. Only trusted devices retain access to the relevant encryption keys, leaving Apple unable to decrypt that protected content for investigators.

Without ADP, those additional categories revert to standard protection: the data remains encrypted, but Apple holds the keys and can disclose content in response to valid legal demands. Some categories remain end-to-end encrypted regardless.
Apple has an explainer on what data types remain end-to-end encrypted, even without ADP enabled, and those that are not.
What the judgment does not confirm
While the IPT's judgment confirms that the Home Office served Apple with a TCN, judges have yet to decide whether key details about the case can be made public.

"Although there has been extensive media coverage and public statements about the existence of a technical capability notice, there has been no publication of its precise content," the judgment stated. "All parties recognize that there may be matters of detail that must be kept secret in order to preserve national security and the public interest.

"We agree that it would be damaging to national security if all of the material (including the content of the technical capability evidence, and the evidence of Apple and the respondent) were publicly disclosed.

"That does not mean every detail must be kept secret in order to preserve national security. There may be some information that could be disclosed publicly without damaging national security. It is not, however, practical to determine the precise boundaries now."
The parties are working toward a substantive hearing in the first half of 2027. Apple's first challenge was dismissed following a "change in circumstances," and it filed a second claim in July 2026.
The Financial Times reported in October 2025 that the UK had replaced its original notice with a new order focused on British users.
The proceedings also include a separate challenge to the TCN regime brought by Liberty, Privacy International, and two individuals.

A government spokesperson said: "Terrorists, child abusers and organized crime groups cannot be allowed to operate beyond the reach of the law. The right to privacy is crucial but it should not come at the expense of the safety of the British public.

"A judge can authorize access to a criminal's home, a parcel they've sent, or a car they drive. The online world is no different. These powers are subject to strict safeguards and the government never has direct access to a company's communications systems or data.

"Apple has been helping the police and intelligence agencies pursue criminals and bring them to justice for several years, in accordance with the law. This Technical Capability Notice simply requires that they maintain the ability to do so.
"Decisions affecting the safety of the British public must be made by democratically elected governments and independent judges, not in the boardrooms of technology companies."
Apple did not immediately respond to our request for comment. ®

59f6988b6f8c610c: JURF AL-SAKHAR: Iraqi security forces will deploy in Jurf al-Sakhar, a stronghold of the Kataib Hezbollah armed group, on Friday, security officials told a press conference, under a compromise deal designed to ease tensions with Iran's most powerful Shi'ite militia ally in the country.

Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi earlier this week ordered security forces to prepare to move against Kataib Hezbollah, which officials accused of running an oil smuggling network siphoning state-owned oil worth hundreds of millions of dollars.
Under the deal, brokered by Shi'ite politicians, Kataib members were expected to withdraw to other parts of Iraq, a major oil producer and ally of both the US and Iran.
Kataib Hezbollah (Battalions of the Party of God), branded a terrorist group by the US, has rejected the smuggling accusations.
So far, nine senior security and oil officials have been dismissed following an investigation focused on Jurf al-Sakhar in Babil province, a Kataib stronghold about 50km south of Baghdad.
Any direct confrontation with Iran's heavily armed militia allies in Iraq could be risky.

After one of Zaidi's predecessors ordered a similar crackdown on militias five years ago, the prime minister's Baghdad home was hit in a drone strike that authorities described at the time as an assassination attempt.

US president Donald Trump has pressured Zaidi to disarm the militias that have struck US troops and facilities in Saudi Arabia and the UAEs in solidarity with Tehran since the US and Israel launched attacks on Iran at the end of February.
Kataib Hezbollah and other militias have refused to hand over their weapons to the state.
Pro-Iranian militias, including Kataib Hezbollah, enjoy a semi-official status in Iraq, which critics say encourages them to act with impunity.
A shadowy group with no announced leadership structure, Kataib Hezbollah has thousands of hardened fighters.
It forms several battalions in Iraq's Popular Mobilization Forces (PMF), a grouping of armed factions set up in 2014 to fight Islamic State and subsequently recognised as an official security force.
Fighters receive state salaries and Kataib Hezbollah members, including some designated as terrorists by the US, hold senior positions in the PMF.

While it is technically under the command of Iraq's prime minister as part of the PMF, the group often operates outside the chain of command and has defied and challenged government statements calling for an end to attacks on US forces.
Kataib has its own political party, called Huquq, or Rights, with five lawmakers.

An Iraqi official report said the group also generates cash through businesses such as construction, housing, trade, tourism and currency exchange, though the group denies this and says it is dedicated to security.

In August, Iraqi special forces reporting directly to the prime minister arrested the intelligence chief of the Iran-aligned faction Harakat al-Nujaba on accusations of involvement in drone attacks against US interests.
The detention, which lasted 48 hours, triggered ​threats of retaliation from the group and prompted intervention by senior Shi'ite politicians who helped defuse tensions.
A week later, Iraqi special forces arrested ​four militia members over allegations they facilitated attacks on US interests.

03f1abc6a1d1c8b3: PETALING JAYA: Sabah Pakatan Harapan (PH) hopes the federal government will settle the remaining RM900 million interim payment relating to the 40% special grant before the state legislative assembly sitting begins on Dec 4.
Sabah PH chairman Mustapha Sakmud said this was important to enable the allocation to be included in the state government's revenue and spent on the needs of the people next year, Bernama reported.

"RM600 million was paid earlier, and another RM900 million is now in the process of being gazetted, bringing the total to RM1.5 billion," he told reporters after chairing a Sabah PH leadership meeting in Kota Kinabalu today.
Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim announced on Oct 7 that Sabah would receive an interim special grant of RM1.5 billion this year.

Anwar, who is also the finance minister, said Putrajaya and the Sabah government were also working towards a permanent formula for calculating the state’s entitlement to its share of federal revenue, as provided for in the Federal Constitution.
Mustapha said today's PH meeting also proposed that the gazettement of interim payments be implemented progressively, with the payment amount increased each year.

He said the proposal took into account revenue generated by federal agencies in Sabah, with the payment amount to be negotiated and mutually agreed upon by the state and federal governments until a final formula for the 40% special grant is reached.

On another matter, he also said Sabah PH hoped the federal government would expedite amendments to Article 46 of the Federal Constitution to enable the proposed increase in parliamentary seats for Sabah and Sarawak to be realised.

Mustapha said the move was important to uphold the spirit of the Malaysia Agreement 1963 (MA63), particularly in ensuring adequate representation for Sabah and Sarawak through the principle of one-third of the seats in the Dewan Rakyat.
He said the constitutional amendments must be implemented before the Election Commission begins its review and the process of redelineating electoral constituencies.
On preparations for the 16th general election, Mustapha said Sabah PH was determined to defend the three parliamentary seats it had previously won, namely Sepanggar, Kota Kinabalu and Sandakan.
At the same time, the coalition was identifying several other potential constituencies to contest without affecting the harmonious cooperation with its component partners in the state government.
Meanwhile, Mustapha announced the appointment of Ruji Ubi as the new Sabah PH secretary.

89b3eebc5418d8ca: KUALA LUMPUR: Police detained three men and seized health, cosmetic and food products worth RM1.27 million in a raid on a logistics premises in Banting, Selangor, yesterday.

The operation, codenamed Op Taring Dosej, was conducted at 12.10pm by the Bukit Aman Wildlife Crime Bureau/Special Intelligence Investigation, under the Internal Security and Public Order Department, with several enforcement agencies.

Bukit Aman Wildlife Crime Bureau/Special Intelligence Investigation commander Senior Assistant Commissioner Datuk Mohd Zaki Ashar said those detained were a local man believed to be the company owner and two Bangladeshi employees.

Checks uncovered 1,044 boxes of health and cosmetic products, 1,300 bottles of supplements and health products, 38 boxes of tremella soup products, 65 boxes of coenzyme Q10 products, as well as various tea-based food and beverage products and snacks.
"All seized items have been handed over to the respective enforcement agencies for further action and investigation under their respective jurisdictions," he said in a statement today.

The total value of the seizure was estimated at RM1.27 million, with the Health Ministry accounting for the bulk at RM1.26 million. The Kuala Langat District Health Office seized items worth RM5,167, while the Domestic Trade and Cost of Living Ministry accounted for RM4,745.

The operation also involved the Selangor Health Ministry's Pharmacy Division, the Customs Department's Klang branch, the Kuala Langat District Health Office, the Domestic Trade and Cost of Living Ministry and the Kuala Langat Municipal Council (MPKL).
The district health office issued two compounds totalling RM4,500, while MPKL issued another two amounting to RM2,000.
The case is being investigated under the Immigration Act 1959/63, Control of Drugs and Cosmetics Regulations 1984, Trade Descriptions Act 2011, Food Act 1983 and related regulations.
Zaki said police would continue to intensify enforcement and intelligence operations to curb smuggling and the distribution of illicit goods.

976ae5489e5f8fa2: PETALING JAYA: Dagang NeXchange Bhd (DNeX) bucked the trend as its shares jumped nearly 13% even as the selloff in technology stocks gained momentum today.

Its shares rose as much as 5 sen or 12.8% to 44 sen before finishing the day up 7.7% at 42 sen, valuing the technology group at RM1.48 billion. It was the most traded stock on Bursa Malaysia with 95.37 million shares changing hands. The stock is up 35% year to date.

While DNeX was keeping its head above the water, other tech stocks dropped sharply today. The Bursa Malaysia Technology Index fell 5% while the FBM KLCI slid to 15-month low, tracking the overnight tech selloff on Wall Street.

Among the major tech companies, UWC Bhd tumbled 9% to a low of RM5.30 while ViTrox Corp Bhd, the largest tech company by market capitalisation, fell as much as 8% to RM8.55. Malaysian Pacific Industries fell 8.2% to an intraday low of RM33.50, its lowest level in seven months.
DNeX garnered investors' attention after announcing its third quarter net profit surged 255% to RM42.63 million from RM12.02 million a year ago, thanks to a rebound in its semiconductor business.

Revenue for the quarter increased 11.2% to RM297.04 million from RM267.16 million a year earlier. For the nine months ended Sept 30, 2026, core profit jumped 188.6% to RM86.1 million while revenue increased 2.7% to RM849.4 million.
The robust earnings performance was mainly attributed to the turnaround at its 60%-owned semiconductor wafer foundry SilTerra Malaysia Sdn Bhd, and its ongoing cost optimisation initiatives.

The semiconductor segment posted a core pre-tax profit of RM60.9 million, compared to a core loss before tax of RM52.8 million a year ago. Higher average selling prices, better product mix, and AI/data centre demand – especially silicon photonics – supported earnings growth at SilTerra.

In its bourse filing yesterday, DNeX said the long-term outlook for the semiconductor industry remains positive despite evolving trade and tariff policies potentially influencing near-term conditions.

It noted the recent settlement of a years-long legal and arbitration dispute with its partner in SilTerra, Tethystronics Technologies Co Ltd, has opened the path for it to focus on the unit's next phase of growth.
DNeX is a global technology company operating in three business divisions namely technology, energy, and information technology.

f94be9a5995b7d21: KUALA LUMPUR: Evidence stored by CyberSecurity Malaysia in the case involving former Petronas manager Mohd Khairul Akmal fully complied with international standards set by the American Society of Crime Laboratory Directors (ASCLD), the Sessions Court heard today.
CyberSecurity Malaysia Senior Digital Forensic Analyst Abdul Wafi Abdul Rahman, 38, said the agency's internal chain-of-custody procedures applied only within its forensic laboratory.

"The internal chain of custody applies only within the laboratory, involving the recipient, storekeeper and analyst. It does not include police investigating officers. These procedures apply only to internal processes after the exhibits have been handed over to us," he said.

The seventh prosecution witness was responding to questions during re-examination by Deputy Public Prosecutor Noor Syafina Mohd Radzuan in the trial of Mohd Khairul Akmal, who is charged with attempting to disclose Petronas' business report and financial structure to Petroleum Sarawak Bhd (Petros) on June 8, 2024.

Yesterday, Abdul Wafi told the court that he had examined a laptop belonging to the accused, two mobile phones and a USB drive between Dec 19, 2024 and Jan 24, 2025 to determine whether they contained any information related to the alleged attempt to transmit the documents.

Meanwhile, Abdul Wafi said he did not trace the location of Mohd Khairul Akmal's laptop, which was allegedly used in an attempt to send confidential information on the national oil company's business and financial structure to Petros, as this was the responsibility of telecommunications companies.

"It is not the responsibility of CyberSecurity Malaysia or myself to trace the location of the perpetrator or the whereabouts of the exhibits within the country, as that is the responsibility of telecommunications companies," he said.

He also said he did not analyse internet connection records in the laptop's event log when preparing the digital forensic report, as this was not within the scope of the investigation requested by the investigating officer.
"If the laptop had used an internet hotspot registered under another individual's name on the date of the incident, the connection activity should have been recorded in the log," he said.

Mohd Khairul Akmal, 41, is charged with attempting to disclose a document entitled 'Q1 2024 Upstream Business Performance Operational & Financial' to Petros, which he had obtained in the course of his duties as Petronas Business Unit Performance Manager, at a condominium unit in Jalan Pinang here, between 3.19 pm and 3.21 pm on June 8, 2024.

The charge is framed under Section 203A(1) of the Penal Code, read together with Section 511 of the same Code. Upon conviction, Section 203A(1) provides for a maximum fine of RM1 million or imprisonment for up to one year, while Section 511 provides for imprisonment of up to half the maximum term prescribed under Section 203A(1).
The trial before Judge Mazuliana Abdul Rashid continues on Feb 9 next year. – BERNAMA
5cf668c0a913c7dc: TP-Link, which may be the top provider of wireless routers for US homes and small businesses, isn't allowed to sell its latest Wi-Fi routers in the US. The Trump administration imposed a sweeping ban on foreign-made consumer routers in March 2026, and TP-Link hasn't been able to obtain an exemption.

The rules prevent the import or sale of all new router models that are manufactured, assembled, designed, or developed outside the US. The Trump administration has control over which router makers receive special permission to import and sell new products through a waiver-review process involving the Federal Communications Commission, the Department of Defense, and the Department of Homeland Security.

While some of its competitors have obtained exemptions to the ban, TP-Link appears to be having a hard time making its case to government officials. Its routers approved before the March 2026 ban remain available for sale in the US, but its newly released Wi-Fi 8 routers cannot be imported or sold.

5ec571d1b4008e30: KUALA LUMPUR: A 1987 Cantopop classic by veteran Hong Kong singer George Lam Chi Cheung has made a surprise appearance on the neon-lit streets of Vice City in Grand Theft Auto VI (GTA 6).
Players exploring Rockstar Games' newly launched blockbuster were stunned to hear Lam's "Dare to Love, Dare to Do" spinning on the in-game radio station, Kaleidoscope FM.
According to Hong Kong media outlet HK01, gamers quickly took to Threads to share clips after unexpectedly catching Lam's unmistakable vocals while cruising through the virtual metropolis.
The Easter egg has been a nostalgic treat for fans who grew up during Cantopop's golden era.
Keen-eared listeners also spotted an amusing link between the track's lyrics and GTA 6's famously chaotic traffic.
One verse describes cars weaving through rain-slicked streets, pedestrians strolling by and traffic lights urging drivers onward — scenes that feel right at home in the Grand Theft Auto universe.
And here is the fun twist: the track is actually a Cantonese adaptation of American rock band Starship's 1987 chart-topper, "Nothing's Gonna Stop Us Now".
Starship's original anthem became a global smash after featuring in the romantic comedy Mannequin, starring Kim Cattrall of Sex and the City fame.
Featuring Cantonese lyrics penned by Poon Wai Yuen, Lam's version went on to become an enduring classic in Hong Kong.
1bf32a8c4d089fbe: TAWAU: "Muhammad Nor Fazryn always looked after his younger sister, wherever he went. They were inseparable. Sadly, neither made it out of the fire."
That was the heartbreaking account of their aunt, Noreen Malvine, 37, following the deaths of the siblings, aged 13 and 10, in a house fire at Taman Ria 11 here early today.

Noreen said her nephew, Muhammad Nor Fazryn Norman, and his 10-year-old sister, Nurailin Nathania, who was autistic, were trapped in an upstairs room of their double-storey terrace house when the fire broke out about 6am.
The room's windows were fitted with security grilles, leaving the children with no way out, she said.
Describing Nor Fazryn as an intelligent and protective older brother, Noreen said he was particularly attentive to Nurailin, whom he rarely left alone.

She said the children's mother, Nor Fazrina Edayu Faisal, had tried desperately to reach them but was eventually forced to escape through a second-floor bedroom window with her three other children when the roof collapsed.
"My sister-in-law fractured her spine when she jumped, while one of her children developed asthma after inhaling the thick smoke," she said.
Noreen said she took the injured mother and her three children to Tawau Hospital, while other family members continued searching for the two missing siblings.
The family later received confirmation that both children had been found dead.
She said Nor Fazrina Edayu was in stable condition but remained hospitalised for treatment. Her husband was making his way back to Tawau from his workplace in Kota Kinabalu.
Tawau Fire and Rescue Station chief Jemishin Ujin said the department received an emergency call at 6.13am and arrived at the scene nine minutes later.
"Upon arrival, we estimated that 70 per cent of the double-storey terrace house was already engulfed in flames.
"Firefighters used water from the fire engine's tank and a fire hydrant to put out the blaze before finding the two children dead in a room," he said.
The cause of the fire is still under investigation.

MN Holdings said it will pursue further opportunities in renewable energy projects, leveraging its existing technical capabilities and project execution experience.
Beyond its core engineering and construction business, the company is also exploring strategic equity investments in renewable energy projects.
"We believe this approach will support a more diversified earnings base and strengthen the company's long-term growth prospects," it said.

Beliau berpandangan pelaksanaan peraturan secara menyeluruh boleh menjejaskan kebebasan berniaga dan operasi peniaga bukan Islam yang tidak tertakluk kepada kewajipan solat Jumaat.

7896629aec4c6091: TAWAU: Pengorbanan seorang abang berusia 13 tahun yang setia menjaga adik perempuannya berusia 10 tahun yang menghidap autisme mengundang sebak apabila mereka ditemukan rentung dalam kebakaran rumah di Taman Ria 11 pagi tadi.

Ibu saudara mangsa, Noreen Malvine berkata, Muhammad Nor Fazryn Norman dan adiknya Nurailin Nathania gagal menyelamatkan diri selepas terperangkap di bilik kedua rumah teres dua tingkat itu yang dipasang jeriji.

“Ke mana-mana sahaja, dia (Muhammad Nor Fazryn) yang urus Nurailin dan mereka memang sentiasa bersama. Ketika tidur pun dia yang jaga, mereka satu bilik tetapi kedua-duanya tidak sempat menyelamatkan diri.
“Muhammad Nor Fazryn abang yang bijak, pelindung dan sentiasa mengutamakan adik-adiknya, terutama Nurailin,” kata wanita berusia 37 tahun itu.

Noreen berkata, adik iparnya, Nor Fazrina Edayu Faisal cuba menyelamatkan kedua-dua mangsa, namun terpaksa menyelamatkan diri dengan terjun melalui tingkap bilik di tingkat dua bersama-sama tiga lagi anaknya apabila bumbung rumah itu runtuh.
“Akibatnya, adik ipar saya cedera dan retak tulang belakang manakala seorang anaknya mengalami asma akibat kepulan asap yang tebal,” katanya.

Noreen kemudiannya membawa Nor Fazrina Edayu dan ketiga-tiga anaknya ke Hospital Tawau untuk mendapatkan rawatan lanjut sementara ahli keluarga lain mencari Fazryn dan Nurailin sebelum dimaklumkan mengenai penemuan mayat kedua-dua mangsa.

Noreen berkata, Nor Fazrina Edayu kini dalam keadaan stabil namun masih menerima rawatan di hospital dan tidak dapat ke unit forensik untuk melihat jenazah kedua-dua anaknya berikutan kecederaan pada kaki yang menyukarkannya bergerak, walaupun menyuarakan hasrat itu menerusi panggilan video.
Suami Nor Fazrina Edayu, yang juga adik Noreen, kini dalam perjalanan pulang ke Tawau dari tempat kerjanya di Kota Kinabalu.
Dalam pada itu, Noreen memaklumkan bahawa kebakaran itu dipercayai berpunca daripada litar pintas, namun punca sebenar kejadian disiasat pihak berkuasa.

Terdahulu, Ketua Balai Bomba dan Penyelamat (BBP) Tawau Jemishin Ujin berkata, ketika kejadian, terdapat enam mangsa terlibat, namun empat daripadanya berjaya keluar menyelamatkan diri sebelum pasukan bomba menemukan kedua-dua mangsa dalam keadaan rentung di bilik tingkat atas kediaman itu.
63147ea43dcbe202: NOWY LIPOWIEC: Russia violated Poland's airspace overnight with three objects that were likely two missiles and a drone, the Polish defence minister said on Friday, as he denounced what he called a "provocation" from Moscow.
The Russian embassy in Warsaw did not immediately respond to an emailed request for comment.
"There has been a violation of Polish airspace and an incursion by objects from the Russian Federation," defence minister Wladyslaw Kosiniak-Kamysz told a news conference.
"There was an Kh-101 missile... In the second case, one can also speak of a missile; in the third, it was most likely a jet-powered drone," he said.
The incursions happened as Poland was set to hold military exercises of the 'Coalition of the Willing' of Ukraine's allies on Friday.

"These exercises, combined with the presence of defence ministers from France, the UK, and the Baltic states — along with eight chiefs of staff, including those from our key allies — suggest that the convergence of these events is no accident," Kosiniak-Kamysz said.
He said that the exercises would go ahead and also said Poland would ask Nato for more support in securing the alliance's eastern flank.
ca34ca01f3645293: KUALA SELANGOR: Flood victims have been advised to register with the authorities immediately, whether they are staying at temporary relief centres or in their own homes, to ensure they do not miss out on assistance.
Women, Family and Community Development Minister Datuk Seri Nancy Shukri said registration was crucial to ensure victims' details were recorded and aid could be distributed efficiently.
"We have channelled all the information, except for those who may have been left out due to timing and other factors.

"Whether they move to relief centres or remain at home, they still need to register so that we have their details on record. Those who register late may take a little longer to receive assistance," she said.
She was speaking after visiting flood victims at the relief centre at Sekolah Kebangsaan (SK) Dato' Maharaja Lela in Kampung Parit Omar, Jeram, today.
Also present were Selangor Social Welfare Department director Azmir Kassim and Kuala Selangor district officer Mohd Raiz Radzuan.
Nancy said the department was prepared for a possible increase in the number of evacuees should the flood situation worsen.
She said that 25 counsellors from the department and the Malaysian Board of Counsellors were on standby to provide psychosocial support to flood victims in Selangor.
A total of 1,817 victims from 503 families were reported to be staying at 14 relief centres across the state.

Nancy had previously told the Dewan Rakyat that flood victims who remained at home were also eligible to apply for the Bantuan Wang Ihsan compassionate aid, provided they registered with the authorities.

f372a07294c20d82: KOTA KINABALU: Sabah Pakatan Harapan (PH) will defend the three parliamentary seats it currently holds while exploring opportunities to contest additional seats in the 16th General Election (GE16).
Its chairman, Datuk Mustapha Sakmud, said the three seats were Sepanggar, which he represents, and Kota Kinabalu and Sandakan, currently held by DAP representatives.
He said Sabah PH's leadership had agreed to retain the seats as its baseline position during negotiations with other parties and coalitions ahead of the election.
"Our basic decision is to defend Sepanggar, Kota Kinabalu and Sandakan.
"We are also looking at the potential to contest other seats without jeopardising our cooperation with other partners," he told a press conference after a PH Sabah meeting here today.
Also present were Sabah Amanah chairman Datuk Lahirul Latigu, Sabah DAP deputy chairman Datuk Chan Foong Hin and Sabah PH secretary Datuk Ruji Ubi.
Mustapha declined to identify the additional seats Sabah PH was eyeing or disclose how many were under consideration.
He said formal negotiations with other political partners, particularly Gabungan Rakyat Sabah (GRS), had yet to begin.
"There have been no formal discussions with GRS so far, only informal engagements," he said.
On Sabah Barisan Nasional's (BN) proposal to establish a Muafakat Sabah pact with GRS, Mustapha said it was a view that the coalition was entitled to express.
At GE15 in November 2022, Sabah PH contested 24 parliamentary seats, with PKR fielding the most candidates at 10, followed by DAP with seven.
The coalition won three seats – Sepanggar, Kota Kinabalu and Sandakan.
Two other seats, Penampang and Tuaran, were also won under the PH banner but were represented by the United Progressive Kinabalu Organisation (Upko), which has since left the coalition.
3f255105f80753c0: PETALING JAYA: Melaka PKR acting chief Adam Adli has reprimanded Melaka DAP chief Khoo Poay Tiong for criticising the Kuala Terengganu city council's (MBKT) directive requiring commercial premises to close during Friday prayers, saying that it is a state matter with a clear religious basis.
He advised Khoo to respect the laws of the respective states as well as religious sensitivities in such matters, noting that the issue was fundamentally a matter of state administration.
“Even if we have differing opinions on the basis for enacting laws, they are still founded on the principle of majority consent.

“Terengganu's people have given their legislature and executive the mandate to enact such laws. We must respect that mandate just as we expect others to respect the mandate given to us,” he said in a statement today.

Adam noted that Islam requires Muslim men to suspend business activities during Friday prayers. “This is not merely a cultural practice or custom but a religious obligation, directly related to the observance of worship,” he said.
He called on Khoo to retract the statement and issue an apology, saying discussions on such matters must be based on an understanding of the law, religious obligations and community sensitivities.
Khoo drew flak from Facebook users earlier today for a post criticising the directive and the RM2,000 fine and one year's imprisonment faced by those who violate it.

Noting that MBKT also has the authority to revoke business licences and order the closure of the premises concerned, he said it reflected the impact of PAS's conservative religious policies on public governance.
Khoo said applying such regulations uniformly to all businesses would affect the business freedom and lifestyles of non-Muslims.
9785d743388736b5: DHAKA: Fresh arson attacks erupted in Bangladesh on Friday as authorities restored communications with the hometown of convicted former prime minister Sheikh Hasina, after days of unrest over her planned return from exile.

Hasina, 79, has vowed to return to Bangladesh in December from India, despite being sentenced to death in absentia for crimes against humanity over a deadly crackdown during the 2024 uprising that ousted her.
Hasina's former ruling party, the Awami League, whose activities are now banned, called for strikes this week to mark the anniversary of the day Hasina received her death sentence.
Hundreds of paramilitary troops have been deployed to contain the unrest, in which at least three people have been killed.
A petrol bomb was hurled at the residence of a junior foreign minister, Humaiun Kobir, in the northeastern city of Sylhet on Friday, police said.
Kobir said Dhaka would deal with attacks "very firmly".
"It is not possible to bring back a 'fled terrorist' by throwing petrol bombs," he told reporters on Friday.
Hasina has said repeatedly she wants to return next month, telling AFP in an email this week that she was "fully aware" she could be hanged.
Attackers also set fire to the home of a former junior foreign minister from the Awami League in Rajshahi on Thursday.
Protesters wielding machetes also torched a police station in Gopalganj, Hasina's political stronghold, the same day. Communications have since been restored.
Police said 124 people linked to the Awami League had been arrested in the capital Dhaka over the past 24 hours, without providing further details.
The family home of Nobel laureate and former interim leader Muhammad Yunus in the port city of Chittagong was also targeted in an arson attack.
Grameen Bank, founded by Yunus, said more than 20 of its branches had been targeted in arson attacks this month.

5603e8838afada89: BATU PAHAT: "My younger brother once promised us he would look after our mother. He kept that promise until their final day."
Those were the heartbreaking words of Abdul Hafiz Abd Muthaliff, 44, who lost his mother and younger brother after their rented house in Kampung Parit Raja Darat was gutted by fire early today.
His mother, Jamilah Bebe Abd Rahman, 63, and brother, Abdul Rahim Abdul Muthaliff, 36, were found burnt to death in their respective bedrooms.
Hafiz said he received the devastating news at 3.35am after being contacted by a relative at 2.45am.
"He called me and said, 'Hafiz, be strong. Your mother's house is on fire.'
"At first, he could not confirm whether anyone was inside. But when he later told me there were people in the house, I rushed here.
"I was so overwhelmed that I could no longer drive and had to ask another younger brother to help," he said when met at the forensic unit of Hospital Sultanah Nora Ismail (HSNI) here today.
Hafiz said he last spoke to his mother on Wednesday, when she called him twice, in the morning and again at night.
He said she had sounded particularly cheerful and even spoke of celebrating Hari Raya Aidilfitri together next year.
"She was so happy that day. She even said she wanted to celebrate Hari Raya with me next year. I never imagined that would be among our last conversations.
"Last night, my brother also sent a TikTok message to my youngest child, asking what the child was doing and enquiring about me and my wife. He also asked when we would be coming over.
"We had no idea it would be his final message," he said.

Meanwhile, Jamilah Bebe's daughter, Jabeera, 40, said losing her mother and younger brother in the same tragedy was particularly devastating, especially as the family had lost an aunt just a week earlier.
"All this while, we only read news about such tragedies happening to other families. This time, it has happened to our own.
"I accept what has happened. May Allah place them both in paradise," she said.
In a statement, Batu Pahat district police chief Assistant Commissioner Shahrulanuar Mushaddat Abdullah Sani said the deaths of the two victims had been classified as sudden deaths.
He said the fire was believed to have broken out while both victims were asleep in their respective bedrooms.

99ee32c4a8b5fc5c: SEREMBAN: Negri Sembilan Menteri Besar Datuk Ismail Lasim has declared the April 19 proclamation seeking to remove Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir as the state's ruler invalid, saying it will not be gazetted.

He also reaffirmed his allegiance to Tuanku Muhriz, declaring that the state government would neither recognise another individual as Yang di-Pertuan Besar nor support any attempt to challenge the ruler's position.
"The state government will not recognise anyone else as Yang di-Pertuan Besar or revive the April 19 proclamation or any related documents.
"I reaffirm that Tuanku Muhriz remains the legitimate Yang di-Pertuan Besar of Negri Sembilan," he told a press conference at the Menteri Besar's official residence here today.
The proclamation, issued amid a dispute involving the state's traditional ruling chiefs, or Undang, sought to depose Tuanku Muhriz and replace him with Tuanku Nadzaruddin Tuanku Ja'afar.

The Attorney-General's Chambers had previously declared the move unconstitutional, while the Dewan Keadilan dan Undang (DKU), the state's royal and customary council, maintained that Tuanku Muhriz remained the legitimate ruler.
Ismail made the declaration after an audience with Tuanku Muhriz at Istana Hinggap this morning. He was appointed Menteri Besar on Aug 2.
Also present at the palace were Undang Luak Rembau Datuk Hassan Ab Hamid, Undang Luak Sungai Ujong Datuk Muhammad Faris Johari and Undang Luak Jelebu Datuk Azrin Khairi.
Ismail said he would uphold the State Constitution and recognise the powers vested in the DKU.

"With the Quran as my witness, I swear to respect and pledge my loyalty to the Yang di-Pertuan Besar of Negri Sembilan and the royal institution, uphold and safeguard the sovereignty of the State Constitution, and recognise the powers vested in the Dewan Keadilan dan Undang," he said.
He also pledged not to allow any state assemblyman, government department, agency or official to take action that could undermine the ruler's sovereignty, position, powers, rights or privileges.

Ismail acknowledged that Datuk Mubarak Dohak and Datuk Maarof Mat Rashad had ceased to hold the positions of Undang Luak Sungai Ujong and Undang Luak Jelebu, respectively, in accordance with their customary laws.
He said Datuk Abdul Rahim Yasin had never been validly appointed Undang Luak Rembau as the required customary installation ceremony had not been completed.
"These three individuals therefore have no legal authority to exercise any powers under Article 10 of the Negri Sembilan State Constitution 1959," he said.
Ismail said matters concerning the appointment, succession or removal of traditional ruling chiefs would be referred to the DKU under Article 16(2) of the State Constitution, where necessary.
He also pledged to recognise and implement all decisions made by the council, including having them gazetted promptly where required.
"I undertake, without reservation, to recognise and implement all decisions of the Dewan, whether already made or to be made," he said.
The state government would also withdraw official recognition, allowances, residences, staff and other privileges from individuals whom the DKU had determined no longer held the office of Undang.
Those recognised by the council, meanwhile, would receive the facilities and privileges attached to their positions without delay.
"These facilities, recognition and privileges will be provided immediately," he said.

b6f28c6c829ce1b8: A Windows 11 passkey bug can leave Android phones announcing that authentication failed even when it succeeded. Microsoft has now released a fix for versions 25H2 and 26H2.

The problem occurs when users sign in on a Windows 11 PC using a passkey stored on an Android phone. Scan the QR code, and the Android device might display the message: "Something went wrong. Restart the process on your other device and try again."

Except it might not have gone wrong at all. Microsoft's guidance explains: "In cases where authentication completes successfully on the Windows device, the error message on the Android device is not supposed to appear and can be safely ignored."

Cross-device authentication lets users sign in on one device using a passkey held on another, without typing a password or copying a verification code. Microsoft says the issue affects operations using Microsoft Authenticator and Google Password Manager, and can occur in Edge or Chrome – not just when signing in through Microsoft Entra ID.
Cross-device passkey operations with an iPhone aren't affected.
An authentication system that cries failure after a successful sign-in isn't doing much for user confidence. Nor will it endear itself to support teams fielding the resulting tickets.

Microsoft has included a fix in KB5132057, the optional non-security preview update released on November 19 for Windows 11 25H2 and 26H2. Until affected devices are patched, users can ignore the Android error if authentication has completed successfully on the PC. ®

0a029dd7efd81dc3: PETALING JAYA: Multi-utility company YTL Power has denied allegations that its data centres helped transfer Nvidia graphics processing units (GPUs) to China, saying such news reports are untrue.

YTL Power, a subsidiary of YTL Group, said its data centres provide co-location services in Johor to multiple global customers, including hyperscalers from the US, under arrangements that are compliant with both domestic laws and US trade controls.
It also said the group has worked closely with the investment, trade and industry ministry on its data centre developments and complied with all applicable reporting and import requirements.

"Various press reports have appeared linking YTL to the current controversy surrounding Nvidia, some even implying that the YTL data centres have in some way assisted in the transfer of Nvidia GPUs to Chinese customers.
"These speculative and unsubstantiated reports are completely untrue," YTL Power said in a statement.

On Nov 18, The New York Times reported that YTL Power's data centres in Johor were allegedly part of an arrangement allowing Chinese technology giant Alibaba to remotely access Nvidia chips through a network of regional companies.

According to NYT, Alibaba agreed to become a customer of Megaspeed International, which used the agreement to secure funding to purchase Nvidia chips. Megaspeed subsequently partnered with data centre operators such as YTL to house and operate the chips, it said.
Megaspeed's subsidiary, Speedmatrix, operated the Nvidia chips on Alibaba's behalf at the data centres, the report said.

On Monday, the Trump administration introduced new restrictions on chip exports to overseas data centres that allow Chinese companies to access advanced AI chips to train their artificial intelligence models.
The rules require companies in Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand, Indonesia and Brazil to apply for US export licences for the most advanced chips to prevent their illegal diversion.

fd35d6cbdee6b000: LONDON: William Saliba is ready to return for Premier League leaders Arsenal after a long injury lay-off but Bukayo Saka faces another month on the sidelines, manager Mikel Arteta said on Friday.
Central defender Saliba, who has been suffering with a back problem, has not played since France's World Cup semi-final defeat by eventual winners Spain in July.
But Arteta said that the 25-year-old was ready for selection for Saturday's trip to Newcastle.
"He's ready, he's in good condition," said the Arsenal boss. "We want to ramp up his minutes. He's played actually two games, one (behind) closed doors, and the other one more official.
"He did very well and he's in good condition."

Arteta now has a selection dilemma on his hands as central defender Ezri Konsa, signed from Aston Villa in August, has been one of Arsenal's standout performers this season alongside Gabriel Magalhaes.
The Spaniard told reporters that Saka was making good progress but was likely to be out of action for another four weeks.
The England winger was replaced early in the Gunners' 2-2 draw against Bayern Munich on Oct 21 after suffering a thigh injury.

"We had another test," said Arteta. "He's evolving really well but looks like it's going to be an eight-week injury, more or less, so I think it's four at the moment so it's a while for him to be back with the team."
Midfielder Martin Zubimendi picked up a hamstring injury in Spain's 3-2 Nations League defeat against England last week and Arteta said he would be out for a "few weeks".
Defending champions Arsenal are five points clear of second-placed Brighton at the top of the Premier League.
1baa1a4cb8f82c56: FRANKFURT: German airline Lufthansa plans to cut 1,000 jobs as its turnaround efforts move slower than hoped, with the energy shock from the Iran war adding to headwinds, according to an internal letter seen by AFP on Friday.
The carrier embarked on a cost-cutting programme in 2024 to stem losses but the measures announced so far are "no longer sufficient", according to the letter sent to staff.
"During the first nine months of the year, the airline was losing on average €20 million (US$22 million) a month," it said.

"The year 2026 has set us back: the war in the Middle East, the still very high fuel costs, nine days of strike action and our already very high cost base have intensified the situation," the letter said.
Germany's flagship carrier now plans to cut 1,000 full-time positions at the Frankfurt and Munich airports, amounting to around 2.5% of its roughly 40,000 employees.

Lufthansa, which also operates carriers including Austrian, Swiss and Brussels Airlines, last year announced plans to cut 4,000 jobs across the whole group by 2030, mainly targeting administrative roles.
It was not immediately clear whether the cuts disclosed on Friday were included in this round of layoffs, or in addition. A Lufthansa spokesman declined to give further details.
Despite the woes of the flagship airline, the wider group is in good financial health.
It reported a 30% jump in profits in the July-September period, beating forecasts, boosted by demand for premium tickets on long-haul routes.
However, surging fuel costs since the start of the US war on Iran are weighing on the group, with its annual fuel bill set to come in €2 billion higher this year than in 2025.
972a5e0472632da7: PETALING JAYA: A man who impersonated an aide-de-camp to the Raja Muda of Selangor and was previously sentenced to prison for fraud involving property and luxury vehicle purchases was sentenced to another 27 months' jail and two strokes of the rotan today for similar offences.

Magistrate Wan Noora Nisa Ngadirin handed down the sentence to Al Zulfadly Alias, 40, at the Shah Alam magistrates' court after he pleaded guilty to cheating two victims of RM73,000 in a vehicle auction scam.
The court ordered the prison terms to run consecutively from the dates he was charged with the offences.
Al Zulfadly's fiancée, Nurul Nur Syahirah Kamarudin, 37, pleaded not guilty to the same charges. The court fixed Jan 19 for mention.

The duo were accused of conspiring with a 43-year-old accomplice to deceive a 48-year-old man by falsely claiming that they could facilitate the purchase of a used Honda CR-V for RM33,000, purportedly acquired through an auction held in conjunction with the Asean Summit.

The offence, allegedly committed in Shah Alam between May 13 and 14, was framed under Section 109 of the Penal Code for abetment, read together with Section 420 for cheating, which provides for up to 10 years' imprisonment, whipping and a fine, upon conviction.
Al Zulfadly was sentenced to 12 months' imprisonment and one stroke of the rotan for the offence.

The couple was also jointly charged with deceiving a 43-year-old woman by claiming that they could facilitate the purchase of a used Lexus RX350 for RM40,000, purportedly acquired through the same auction.
The offence, framed under Section 420 of the Penal Code, read together with Section 34, was allegedly committed at Taman Sri Andalas, Shah Alam, between April 13 and 14.
Al Zulfadly was sentenced to 15 months' imprisonment and one stroke of the rotan for the offence.

According to the facts of the case, Al Zulfadly introduced himself to the victims as an ADC to the Raja Muda of Selangor and claimed that he could arrange the purchase of vehicles through an auction at lower prices.
Believing his claims, the victims transferred RM33,000 and RM40,000, respectively, into a bank account belonging to him. However, neither received the vehicles as promised.
The couple was initially charged in the Shah Alam magistrates' court on Nov 12 with cheating involving the sale of an auctioned vehicle worth RM33,000.
The following day, they were charged in the Klang magistrates' court over the RM40,000 vehicle scam. The case was subsequently transferred to the Shah Alam court.

On Nov 16, Al Zulfadly was sentenced to a year's imprisonment and two strokes of the rotan by the Kuala Lumpur magistrates' court after pleading guilty to cheating a celebrity in a property-purchase scam.

The following day, he was sentenced by the Kuala Lumpur sessions court to two years' imprisonment and four strokes of the rotan after being convicted on four counts of cheating a female doctor of RM155,000 in scams involving property and luxury vehicle purchases.

8a241eb950c4a331: KUALA LUMPUR: YTL Power International Bhd today denied allegations linking its Johor data centres to the alleged transfer of Nvidia graphics processing units (GPUs) to Chinese customers.
The group described the reports as speculative and untrue.
YTL Power said its data centre subsidiary YTL Data Centers provides co-location services including space, power, cooling and connectivity to multiple global customers, including US hyperscalers.
It stressed that these arrangements comply with Malaysian laws and US trade controls.
The group added that it has worked closely with the Investment, Trade and Industry Ministry on its data centre developments and met all applicable reporting and import requirements.

The denial comes amid heightened scrutiny over the use of US-made advanced semiconductors, particularly Nvidia GPUs, in overseas data centres and concerns that computing capacity located in third countries could be accessed remotely by Chinese companies.

The US Commerce Department's Bureau of Industry and Security issued an interim final rule on Nov 19 to prevent companies in countries of concern, including China, from accessing large volumes of advanced computing power through data centres overseas.
The new rules impose licensing requirements on certain advanced semiconductor exports to Malaysia, Indonesia, Singapore, Thailand and Brazil.
They also target overseas data centres that provide significant computing capacity to companies headquartered in China or other restricted destinations.

YTL Power said the new rules do not affect its co-location services, as the provisions cited by the group focus on semiconductor importers and providers of computing services to customers in restricted destinations.
It expressed confidence that demand for co-location data centre infrastructure in Malaysia will continue to expand, supported by strong global demand, including from US customers.

YTL Power berkata pihaknya kekal yakin terhadap pertumbuhan industri pusat data Malaysia, didorong permintaan global yang kukuh terhadap infrastruktur berkenaan, termasuk dari AS.

8c77f20b8ca52aae: ANTALYA: Turkey is set to emerge from COP31 with billions of dollars in investment deals, including on green energy, but the chances of an ambitious outcome to curb the world's carbon emissions looked slim as the talks entered what was meant to be their final day.
The country said it has agreed deals and plans worth more than US$26 billion in total since it began hosting the climate conference on Nov 9 in the Mediterranean city of Antalya.
They include a preliminary US$15 billion renewable energy deal with China, US$5.1 billion in financing agreements with development banks, and accords with Saudi Arabia and Canada.
Past hosts of climate conferences have also benefited from the influx of foreign governments and companies that typically accompanies UN talks.
In 2023 the UAE pursued both fossil fuel and renewable energy deals on the sidelines of the Dubai COP.
Turkey did not comment on the deals.
Observers said the agreements, many of them related to clean energy, could help Turkey with its own climate goals, including expanding electrification to help reduce fossil fuel emissions.

"I have long advocated for COP-hosting countries to use their COP as an investment attraction platform. It's your best opportunity," said Li Shuo, a veteran observer of China ​at UN climate talks who heads the China Climate Hub at the Asia Society Policy Institute.
Oyku Senlen, senior researcher at think tank E3G, said the deals aligned with "Turkey's energy transition pathway".
"It should lead the way for Turkey to broker a strong deal out of COP 31," she said.

But a broader international climate deal appears elusive as the delegates from more than 190 countries are divided on central issues, such as climate finance to help the poorest and most vulnerable deal with the impact of a warmer world.
Negotiators have also stripped out any reference to phasing down fossil fuel use from the latest draft agreement.
Although the talks are scheduled to end on Friday, UN conferences have a history of continuing past deadline.

fe954183033f4103: LONDON: British retail sales volumes unexpectedly rose 0.7% in October compared with September, bolstered by a government call for households to stock up on long-life items as well as stronger clothing sales, official figures showed on Friday.
The jump in October sales volumes beat all economists' forecasts in a Reuters poll and lifted the annual growth in sales to a two-month high of 2.3% from 0.4% in September.

"Supermarkets have told us that sales of long-life food items such as tinned food and UHT milk were boosted by the government's 'Be Ready' campaign," Office for National Statistics (ONS) chief economist Grant Fitzner said.
UK households told to keep three days of food and water

Last month, Britain's government advised the public to keep three days of emergency supplies at home, ​a message it said had been hammered home by online computing security flaws, as well as a record-setting summer of heat, drought and wildfires.

Food stores reported a 0.8% rise in sales volumes in October after a 0.3% drop the month before, the ONS said, while cooler weather also boosted sales of autumnal clothes after a warmer than usual September.
There was no immediate market reaction to the data, which retail analysts said shed little light on longer-term trends.
"An unexpected recovery in retail sales in October underlines the current fickle nature of consumer confidence.

"The increase in sales ... is probably a one-off which hides the challenge facing retailers as they head into the crucial festive trading period," said Rajeev Shaunak, head of consumer at accountants MHA.

Consumer sentiment had fallen sharply in October, according to Britain's longest-running measure of it, as rising fuel bills and borrowing costs squeezed households, although November data released earlier on Friday showed a small recovery.

Consumer price inflation rose to a one-year high of 3.6% in October, and the Bank of England forecast it would reach close to 5% in the middle of next year when it raised interest rates for the first time in three years this month.
However, overall economic growth has been stronger than expected this year and recent updates from major British retailers have been mixed.

Clothing and food retailer Marks & Spencer said recent trading had been solid and it entered the Christmas period with momentum, while Primark and Next highlighted a pickup in sales in October when the weather turned colder.

However, JD Sports said its UK sales trend softened in its third quarter versus a soccer World Cup-boosted second quarter, while discounter Poundland considered entering administration, a form of insolvency protection.
a6025882e2e41fb5: SHAH ALAM: Seorang lelaki menyamar sebagai pengawal peribadi sulit (ADC) Raja Muda Selangor, yang sebelum ini dihukum penjara atas kesalahan menipu berhubung pembelian hartanah serta kenderaan mewah, hari ini dipenjara 27 bulan dan dua sebatan oleh Mahkamah Majistret kerana menipu berhubung penjualan dua kenderaan lelong bernilai RM73,000.

Mereka didakwa bersubahat dengan seorang lelaki berusia 43 tahun untuk menipu seorang lelaki berusia 48 tahun dengan memperdayakannya supaya mempercayai bahawa mereka mempunyai keupayaan menguruskan pembelian sebuah kenderaan terpakai jenis Honda CRV, yang kononnya diperoleh menerusi lelongan sempena Sidang Kemuncak Asean pada harga RM33,000.

Pasangan itu didakwa di Mahkamah Majistret Shah Alam pada 12 Nov lalu atas pertuduhan menipu melibatkan urusan jual kenderaan lelong bernilai RM33,000 dan keesokan harinya (13 Nov), mereka didakwa di Mahkamah Majistret Klang atas pertuduhan menipu melibatkan penjualan kenderaan lelong bernilai RM40,000. Kessokannya, lelaki itu sekali lagi dijatuhi hukuman penjara dua tahun dan empat sebatan oleh Mahkamah Sesyen Kuala Lumpur atas empat pertuduhan menipu seorang doktor wanita membabitkan RM155,000 berkaitan pembelian hartanah serta kenderaan mewah.

c1bc16b70ede5f6f: Canonical is targeting Ubuntu 28.04 LTS for the release of its immutable Core Desktop, with a stretch goal of making it the default download for Ubuntu 30.04.

Canonical's VP of engineering, Jon Seager, set out the timetable in his opening keynote at Ubuntu Summit 26.10. Yes, we know, we have heard this before: we reported on his plans last month. But this time, there's the beginning of a release schedule.

Seager said that Ubuntu Core is already out there in tens of thousands of IoT devices – which seems like a modest estimate to us, and to him too, as he quickly added "maybe more." Despite some noise a few years ago, though, what's still missing is the desktop version.
Seager's slides listed three bullet points: that Core Desktop will be "immutable," "composable," and "attestable."

As he put it, they are "taking the whole of the Linux operating system, and cramming the whole thing into snaps." Acknowledging that this is going to be wildly controversial, he said: "This is one for the Redditors."

He's right. There is a lot of resistance to snap, and in direct response, advocacy of the Red Hat-backed Flatpak instead – but we have seen almost none that is based on either system's technical merits. Much of that opposition concerns claims of one being more open than the other. We've looked at how both systems work, and our impression is that the implementation of snap is cleaner, simpler, easier to use, and more comprehensible. Snap does depend on systemd, which Flatpak does not – but only for now. Flatpak NG is in development and will also need everyone's favorite init system.
Ubuntu Core's immutability is not new technology: even Core 16 is now a decade old. It has supported in-place version upgrades since Core 22.

We have reported before that Canonical remains strongly committed to its packaging format, and that commitment seems stronger than ever. Seager continued: "Never has a model like snap confinement been more relevant… we're finally in a position where we can bring this to the desktop."

The core idea of an immutable OS is that "much more of the system is not writable at runtime," meaning that it "can't be messed with once the system has booted." He talked about the same three use cases we discussed last month. The "browser-centric machine" is the company's analog to Google ChromeOS, and he said that it's essentially ready now, suggesting that everyone listening probably has a family member whose computer is basically just a way to use a web browser.

The second was the dedicated games machine, which we interpret as a response to Valve's SteamOS. This edition, he said, would "boot straight to Steam," with "just enough of a shell to launch games." There's also an immutable "development workstation," and here, he offered the example of developers who need to work on some long-unsupported hardware or software, for whom an immutable OS means that you "can't brick your system by installing some weird old dependencies, unmaintained for 20 years."

Another important benefit is "atomic, transactional updates," which he said "brings enormous stability." The terminology comes from the database world: an atomic operation succeeds as a whole or is not applied. The aim is to avoid leaving the system stranded between incompatible package versions, with rollback providing a route back if an update causes trouble.
The "composable" part means assembling the OS from separately packaged components, from desktop environments to underlying services such as PipeWire and fingerprint-reader support.

Here, Seager used an example that spoke to us. He asked: "Ever installed something and watch as it spewed stuff all over your system?" Yes, we have, many, many times. You install one innocent-seeming little component, and it brings in a database, three new server components, and about half of a different desktop environment. We mentioned an example when we described how to customize Xfce a couple of months ago. That time around, in Debian, we found it was safe to install all packages starting with "xfce4-" except "xfce4-dev-tools." Most are tiny panel controls taking just hundreds of kilobytes, but the "dev-tools" package also pulls in several hundred megabytes of compilers, linkers, and other programming tools, totally unrelated to desktop layouts – and once installed, they're surprisingly tricky to remove again.

This is part of the appeal of a composable immutable OS: adding a component need not mean tangling its dependencies into the base system. But easier housekeeping isn't the only attraction. Canonical kept snap packages from its cancelled phone and tablet OS because snaps enable it to maintain a single package of, for instance, Firefox, which will work on all of its different OS versions that are still getting updates. Moving such important external dependencies into isolated snap packages makes it easier and safer to upgrade from one version of the OS to another. Complex sets of dependencies are the main point of failure of OS upgrades, especially when the OS has been used for a while.

This is very much not a solved problem. For instance, Debian version upgrades can be fraught – especially when the installation has decades of history behind it. Debian does at least support version-to-version upgrades. For many years and versions, RHEL did not – which is why we highlighted AlmaLinux's tooling for the task. Zorin OS added version-to-version upgrades in 16.3 just a few years ago. Linux Mint introduced its own upgrade tooling a few years earlier, although it still imposes restrictions.

It's a tough issue to crack. Major enterprise vendors discourage it, and phone OSes are all immutable. Helping with this problem is one of the main reasons snap packaging exists, while Flatpak is almost entirely irrelevant to it.

Seager also stated that Core Desktop would support "multiple desktops from the start." This will not be a GNOME-only project. Indeed, he specifically mentioned a KDE Plasma version, saying: "Plasma is great. People love it. We will have a KDE edition, with rolling Plasma. We will deliver upstream Plasma, as fast as we can." That sounds like a very welcome counterpoint to the LTS version of Plasma 6.6 in Kubuntu 26.04 whose announcement we covered back in August.

For the "attestable" line of the slide, he claimed that Core Desktop was "evolving the way we think about 'trust' on a machine. We have TPM, secure boot, TPM-backed Full Disk Encryption… but they're all bolt-ons." Core Desktop, he added, could "tie this into a hardware root of trust," delivering "verified system integrity." Canonical revived its TPM-backed full-disk encryption system back in 2025, and it arrived in Ubuntu 26.04. Back in January, systemd creator Lennart Poettering launched his startup Amutable, and earlier this month published a technical overview of its new immutable Linux. We suspect Canonical is watching closely, and that this is a hint in that direction.

We were also amused by Seager's mention of another rather niche distro: he said that Core Desktop would deliver "all of the joy that people derive from NixOS, for those with that perverse habit – but for everybody."

Daily preview installation images of Core Desktop will, apparently, be available very soon, in both GNOME and KDE flavors, and he warned that "there be dragons." (That may be a veiled nod to one of founder Mark Shuttleworth's other companies.)

After the promises made in 2023, we'll be watching that timetable closely. "I believe this is the future of Linux," Seager said, promising "a final version by 28.04, released alongside Ubuntu," adding that a "very stretchy stretch goal was by default for 30.04: download from ubuntu.com and you get Core Desktop – unless you ask for the other thing."
For those alarmed by that prospect, he had reassurance: "Ubuntu as you know it today is not going anywhere. There are no plans for the existing distro to go away."

Core Desktop wasn't even the main subject of his keynote. They followed a lengthy excursion into formal logic: definitions, proofs, invariants, and designing software whose behavior can be checked against precisely stated rules. The accompanying slides showed the logos of organizations working in this area, such as Hegel, Antithesis, and the Lean programming language. For now, an entire OS is much too big to formally verify, but subcomponents may be doable – and Canonical is starting with snapd.

He also expressed his satisfaction with the Stonking release, highlighting that it advanced Canonical's move toward Rust-based components, including Rustls and upki – noting that this proved very timely in the light of recent events. The release also delivered the newest available kernel, OpenSSL 4 – which he called a "huge change" – and official RISC-V images. He also called out the Myna speech-recognition feature, saying that it was all in-house, designed and shipped in six months by a team of "about two and a half people." It will form part of the company's plans for what it calls a context-aware desktop. ®
